chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who fights in defense of his property. He said, “Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: Whoever is killed defending his property is in the station of a martyr.”
So I said to him: Is fighting better? He said, “If you do not fight, there is no harm. As for me, if I were there, I would leave it and would not fight.”
And Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq wrote to Abī Muḥammad عليه السلام asking about the brigands, and he wrote back to him, “Kill them.”
Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, or someone else, reported that he wrote to him asking him about the Kurds, and he wrote, “Do not awaken them except by the edge of the sword.”

key_terms.بِحَدِّ السَّيْفِ: by the edge of the sword, indicating armed force
key_terms.شَهِيدٍ: one accorded the rank or station of a martyr
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection
key_terms.قُتِلَ: was killed in the course of the confrontation
key_terms.مَالِهِ: his property or wealth being defended

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhib al-Ahkam say about fighting to defend property and dealing with brigands?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses legal rulings related to defending one’s property and confronting violent aggressors. It reports that one killed defending his wealth has the rank of a martyr, while also indicating that refraining from fighting may be permissible, alongside separate directives regarding brigands and hostile groups.
